approach: Root cause: `refusing_check` (crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-549) is an ordered list of `step!` checks, and none compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria. No rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it, so a reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` is accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k; failed attempt 20261030-060839-1njk). Fix it at that gate: add `check_request_parts` as the last step, so every existing refusal keeps its check name. The round-5 design is kept: the shared `request_own_lines` filter factored out of `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189), Enumerated and Bullet kinds, distinctive-stem coverage, clause-scoped criterion negation, and enforcement by code only. Round 6 changes, one per finding. (F1) terms.rs is now a listed deliverable. (F2) A request sentence outside every part that cites a part's marker defers it on the broad MARKER_NEGATION list (later, out of scope, for now, defer, skip, follow-up...), guarded against a negator such as 'must not be skipped'. The part's own text and unmarked sentences keep the narrow DEFER_PHRASES list. (F3) Alternatives become one group covered by any member; an optional part may be left out. (F4) Bullet parts have marker None, and marker rules apply only to Enumerated parts. (F5) The sza7 fixture names crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs (the timeout file). (F6) Coverage by a deliverable path alone is dropped; a path only adds stems to a criterion that contains it, and generic path words are ignored. (F7) Four Acceptance headings open the bullet section.

decisions.choice: 1. Build `request_parts` on a shared line filter. Factor the loop of `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189-208: ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR and APPROVAL_ANCHOR flags, stop at '## Source' for approved work, drop fenced lines, drop `is_generated_line` lines, terms.rs:62) into `pub(super) fn request_own_lines(request: &str) -> Vec<&str>`. `plain_request_prose` becomes `request_own_lines(request).into_iter().map(plain_line).join("\n")` with identical output. `request_parts` (topics.rs) reads only `request_own_lines` and, for an approved-work request, skips its first line (the proposal title). RequestPart = {marker: Option<String>, kind: Enumerated|Bullet, text, group: Option<usize>, optional: bool}. `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet` stay unchanged. terms.rs is a listed deliverable (finding 1): the brief's Expected deliverables now include it, so the file is in scope.
decisions.reason: Generated and copied text (approved-work '## Source' copies from work_decisions.rs, the root-cause title and 'Cause:' lines from hestia.rs, fenced 'Request:' blocks) holds 'Acceptance:' bullets and numbered lists that must never become parts. One shared filter means a later change to the generated shapes is made once. The plan parses nothing in the 'Introspection ... prevention it proposed:' lines because `is_generated_line` skips them. `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs plan_entry; steward.rs:587) and the corpus pins its bullet counts, so it stays.

rejected.option: Keep a private skip list in `request_parts`
rejected.why: Misses fences and the approved-work '## Source' copy and drifts from terms.rs.

rejected.option: Extend `is_bullet` to read `N)` and `(a)`
rejected.why: Moves plan acceptance of every queued request and the pinned bullet counts.

rejected.option: Read inline sequences from the whole request
rejected.why: Quoted or copied text with markers would become required parts.

decisions.choice: 2. Place `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));` last in `refusing_check`, after `check_reading_references` (checks.rs:549). It returns Ok when `capability` is none or `question` is some, as `check_governance_coverage` does.
decisions.reason: Each existing Refuse case keeps its refusing check; `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on the `check_reading_references` step line and still works. Only Accept cases with explicit parts can change.

rejected.option: Place it early, after `check_criteria_evidence`
rejected.why: It would pre-empt `check_outcome_state` in the delivery cases with `2)` and `(a)` parts.

decisions.choice: 3. Parser kinds (finding 4 and 7). `request_parts` runs over `request_own_lines` with states before / in section / after. Before the heading, Enumerated parts are line-start `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` and inline `(1)..(2)..` or `(a)..(b)..` sequences (start at 1 or a, consecutive, 2+ markers, each marker followed by text with a significant stem; the last part ends at the first '. ' or line end). The Acceptance section opens on a trimmed, case-insensitive line equal to one of `Acceptance:`, `Acceptance criteria:`, `## Acceptance` or `## Acceptance criteria`. Any other heading is a stated limit in the doc comment. In the section, a line starting `-`, `*` or `N.` is a Bullet with marker None (never also Enumerated, no inline scan); `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` lines are Enumerated. Blank and indented lines stay in the section. The section ENDS at the first non-blank line that has no leading whitespace and is not a list line; after that nothing is read as a part. Marker-cited coverage (5c) and every MARKER_NEGATION rule apply only to Enumerated parts, because a Bullet has no marker, so criterion 2's own words 'leaves (3) out ... as a follow-up' do not number bullets by position.
decisions.reason: Findings 4 and 7. Enumerated parts are the failure class; Acceptance bullets are the second introspection's proposal. The two kinds need different stem counts (2 and 1), so a line has exactly one kind. StewardRequest puts a `Files:` line after its bullets (steward.rs:581-585), and a later Notes list or copied block must not become required bullets. Many tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests and no heading; a free-form dash bullet is not a named part.

rejected.option: Only the exact line `Acceptance:` opens the section
rejected.why: Finding 7: hand-written variants leave their bullets unenforced.

rejected.option: Number bullets by position so a marker can cite them
rejected.why: Finding 4: the own-reading case would depend on an unstated choice and criterion 2's '(3) ... follow-up' would cancel itself.

rejected.option: The section never ends, or resumes Enumerated parsing after it
rejected.why: A later Notes or Files list would become required parts.

rejected.option: Treat every dash or star bullet as a part
rejected.why: False refusals over fixtures with free-form bullets.

decisions.choice: 4. Alternatives and optional parts (finding 3). Groups: (i) an inline sequence is one group when the text before its first marker in the same sentence holds 'either', 'one of', 'choose' or 'pick', or when the last marker is preceded by ' or ' / ', or '; (ii) contiguous line-start parts that follow a non-part line holding 'either', 'one of', 'choose' or 'pick' are one group; (iii) a part line ending ' or' groups with the next part. A group is covered when any member is covered, is skipped when every member is skipped (deferred or optional), and the error names the group ('one of (a) ..., (b) ...'). A part is optional, and skipped, when its text after the marker starts with 'optionally' or holds 'if time permits' or 'nice to have'. Groups apply to Enumerated parts only. Known limits (doc comment): an 'or' inside one part's text is not a group; 'either' without markers is not read.
decisions.reason: 'Store it either as (a) a JSON file or (b) a TOML table.' must accept a reading that picks (a). out_of_scope never covers, so without groups the only repair would be a criterion for work not being done.

rejected.option: Treat every (a)/(b) sequence as required parts
rejected.why: Finding 3: refuses a reading that chose one option, with no honest repair.

rejected.option: Let any reading omit parts that contain 'or'
rejected.why: Too wide: 'Add a flag or alias' style parts would never be enforced.

decisions.choice: 5. Stems (`part_stems`), unchanged from round 5 except for paths. Strip a leading `[tag]`; lowercase ASCII alphanumeric words; drop all-digit words and words under 3 letters. For each word w, s = w without one trailing 's' when w is longer than 3. Drop the word when w or s is in FUNCTION_WORDS (the, and, for, not, with, without, unless, are, its, can, all, any, one, add, use, new, via, per, but, has, how, out, was, may, our, you, see, two, who, why, too, now), COMMON_WORDS (topics.rs:157-161) or PART_FILLER (pass, passes, passed, passing, cargo, clippy, fmt, content, behavior). Keep s cut to 6 chars; map `doc` to `docume` (STEM_ALIASES). `stems_match(a,b)`: equal, or the shorter has 4+ chars and is a prefix of the other. Path stems (finding 6): for a deliverable path, split on non-alphanumerics and ignore the words crates, src, core, tests, test, lib, mod, bin, and the extensions rs, md, toml, json, txt, yml, yaml, lock before stemming. The unit test `part_stems_worked_examples` asserts: 'Add the --json flag to status' = {json, flag, statu}; 'Document the flag in the guide' = {docume, flag, guide}; 'Cover the flag with a timeout test' = {cover, flag, timeou, test}; '[content] docs/guide.md describes --json' = {docume, guide, descri, json}; 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' = {test, fail, change}; and the path stems of crates/athena-core/tests/foo.rs = {athena, foo}.
decisions.reason: The filler list applies to the bare word and its singular so gate words add no stems. The alias keeps 'docs/guide.md describes --json' covering '(2) Document the flag in the guide'. Ignoring generic path words means 'crates/athena-core/tests/foo.rs' cannot share the stem 'test' with a dropped test part.

rejected.option: Keep path segments such as crates, core and tests as stems
rejected.why: Finding 6: every repo path carries them, so a test-file path would cover any test part.

rejected.option: Drop the alias and require 4-letter stems
rejected.why: The natural criterion 'docs/guide.md describes --json' would be falsely refused.

decisions.choice: 6. Coverage (finding 6). For each kind with 2+ parts, drop from every part the stems that occur in every part of that kind (fallback to the full set if that empties a part); n is the remaining count; need = min(2,n) for Enumerated, min(1,n) for Bullet; n = 0 is skipped. A part is covered when (a) one usable criterion, pooled with the path stems (decision 5) of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains, shares at least `need` stems with it, or (c) a usable criterion cites the marker of an Enumerated part (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c`; not bare `N)`) and shares at least 1 distinctive stem. Rule (b), a deliverable path alone covers, is REMOVED. A deliverable is required by the existing checks and the error says 'cover it with a deliverable and a criterion'. `out_of_scope` never covers.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 of the brief: a path alone does not cover a part. Dropping shared stems stops a criterion for part (2) covering part (3) through the shared subject 'flag'. The tension is named in the doc comment: stricter refuses more reworded readings, looser misses dropped parts. Athena's replay holds a candidate whose newly refused share exceeds the declared 10% plus the 5-point margin, 15% (replay.rs:296-308).

rejected.option: Keep rule (b) with generic path words removed
rejected.why: Still lets a path cover a part with no criterion, against the brief and introspection 20261029-111106-c3pq.

rejected.option: Assign each criterion to its one best part
rejected.why: More logic and tie rules than dropping shared stems.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text
rejected.why: The summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would look covered.

decisions.choice: 7. Criterion-side negation is scoped to a clause and to the part, as in round 5. DEFER_PHRASES: follow-up job, follow up job, in a follow-up, in a follow up, as a follow-up, as a follow up, separate job, next job, later job, not in this job, deferred to, can wait. CRITERION_NEGATION = DEFER_PHRASES plus out of scope, out-of-scope, deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of. MARKER_NEGATION = CRITERION_NEGATION plus skipped, omitted, excluded, bare later, defer, skip, follow-up, follow up, followup, for now. `negation_hit(criterion, part)` splits the criterion into clauses at '. ', '; ', ', ', ': ' and ' and ', ' but ', ' while ', ' so '. A clause is relevant when it holds a word whose stem matches a distinctive stem of the part, or (MARKER_NEGATION, Enumerated parts only) cites the part's marker. A CRITERION_NEGATION phrase in a relevant clause, or a MARKER_NEGATION phrase in a marker-citing clause, makes the criterion unusable for that part, unless the part's own text holds the phrase. A criterion unusable for one part may cover another. The error lists each ignored criterion with its phrase.
decisions.reason: Criteria here often describe refusal behaviour ('moves it to out_of_scope as a follow-up'); the phrase cancels only next to the part's own subject. 'The timeout test is deferred' still cannot cover part (3); 'status lists skipped checks' still covers '(2) Report skipped checks in status'. Bullets have no marker, so for them only CRITERION_NEGATION in a relevant clause applies.

rejected.option: Count a phrase anywhere in the criterion
rejected.why: Cancels criteria that mention refusal in another clause.

rejected.option: A flat list where skipped, omitted and excluded cancel every criterion
rejected.why: Refuses 'status lists skipped checks'.

decisions.choice: 8. Request-side deferral (finding 2). A part is skipped as deferred when (i) its own text holds a DEFER_PHRASES phrase ('(3) Add a dashboard in a follow-up job'), or (ii) another sentence of `request_own_lines`, taken outside every part span (spans blanked before splitting at '. ', '! ', '? ' and newlines), cites its marker as `(N)`, `N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c` or `item c` and holds any MARKER_NEGATION phrase, which includes 'later', 'out of scope', 'for now', 'defer', 'skip' and 'follow-up'; or (iii) such a sentence holds a DEFER_PHRASES phrase and cites the marker. A sentence is not a deferral when, after removing the phrases that themselves hold 'not' ('not in this job', 'not part of', 'not done', 'not covered'), it still holds not, n't, never or cannot ('Part 2 must not be skipped'). Parts of a text with no marker citation outside the parts are never deferred by (ii). The narrow list applies to a part's own text and to unmarked sentences, so '(2) Reject future timestamps', '(1) List each file separately', '(3) Defer the flush until exit' and '(3) Add a latest-value column' stay required. Stated departure from criterion 4's 'later' example: bare 'later' inside the part's own text (for example '(3) Add the dashboard later') does not defer it; criterion 4 speaks of a sentence outside the part, which is handled by (ii). 'Parts 2 and 3 can come later' cites only part 2 (word-boundary 'part N'); that is a stated limit.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: the same trust the plan gives MARKER_NEGATION when a criterion names the marker applies to a request sentence that names the marker. The marker citation is the guard against stray words. The negator guard prevents 'must not be skipped' from deferring a part.

rejected.option: Narrow DEFER_PHRASES only for request sentences
rejected.why: Finding 2: 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' and 'Part 3 can come later.' would leave the part required and the reader could not follow the request.

rejected.option: Broad list for the part's own text
rejected.why: Exempts real parts such as '(3) Defer the flush until exit'.

decisions.choice: 9. Enforce by code only. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say why information alone is not enough: the reader already sees the request and still deferred part (3) in jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, so a refusal rule is the allowed fix. 'Pass the parsed request parts to the reader' is named as a follow-up, not done here. No prompt is edited (reader budget 1998 of 2000, docs/system-facts.md). The refusal text reaches the reader on its one corrected re-read (reading.rs:738-759).
decisions.reason: No token headroom in the reader prompt, and a prompt line is not a mechanism.

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt
rejected.why: No budget; prose only.

rejected.option: Build the parsed parts into the reader brief now
rejected.why: A larger change across briefs and budgets.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings that reword a part so it shares too few distinctive stems with any criterion; stricter matching refuses more, looser misses dropped parts.
risks.mitigation: Tension named in the doc comment. Bullets need one distinctive stem; n = 0 parts are skipped; filler and gate words are filtered; a marker-citing criterion with one distinctive stem covers an Enumerated part; one criterion pools with the paths it names; the error names the part, the repair and each ignored criterion, and the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The proxy test and the own-reading case guard the common case. The 10% is an estimate; Athena's replay measures it at verification (records/ is absent for the planner).

risks.risk: A request sentence that cites a marker with a broad word is read as a deferral when it is not (for example 'Part 3 must not be skipped', or 'Parts 2 and 3 can come later' naming only part 2).
risks.mitigation: Marker citation is required; a negator guard blocks 'must not be skipped'; the Refuse case `request-parts-request-says-part-must-not-be-skipped` pins it; 'Parts N and M' lists are a stated limit. A missed deferral is refused with text telling the reader to cover the part.

risks.risk: Bare 'later' in a part's own text is not a deferral, so a reading that follows '(3) Add the dashboard later' is refused (stated departure from criterion 4's wording, which speaks of a sentence outside the part).
risks.mitigation: Stated in the doc comment and pinned by `request-parts-part-own-text-later-stays-required`; the request can defer with a sentence naming the marker.

risks.risk: Alternatives grouping misses a form (an 'or' inside one part, 'either' with no markers) so one option is required, or groups too much.
risks.mitigation: Groups need an introducer word or an ' or ' before the last marker; limits are listed in the doc comment; corpus cases cover each form plus a none-covered Refuse.

risks.risk: The shared filter changes `plain_request_prose` output by accident, moving defined-terms results.
risks.mitigation: The helper holds the same loop; `plain_request_prose_is_unchanged_by_the_shared_filter`, the defined-terms corpus cases and `approve_request_has_the_generators_shapes` run in `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: An existing scripted or stored reading whose request has an Acceptance heading or enumerated markers is newly refused, forcing edits outside the listed files (reading.rs:7396, 7743; steward.rs tests; run/tests.rs; drain.rs).
risks.mitigation: Dash bullets count only inside an Acceptance section. The producer runs the listed package tests, repairs the fixture's criteria never the check, and names the file in the report.

risks.risk: A part-like list after the Acceptance section ends, an Acceptance heading written another way, or a part inside a fence is not enforced.
risks.mitigation: A stated narrow rule with the exact four headings in the doc comment; copied text and fences must not become parts.

demonstrations.method: Source-text unit test in the style of `history_fixture_has_one_step_line` (reading.rs:8205-8230). It reads `reading_source()` (reading.rs:1578) and asserts: `pub fn check_request_parts(reading: &Reading, request: &str) -> Result<()>` is defined; the `refusing_check` body has exactly one line equal to `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));`, and it is the last `step!`; the doc comment above the function contains 'does not compare', 'in scope', '20261029-084645-sza7', '20261029-110953-bw7k', '20261030-060839-1njk', 'already sees the request', 'Acceptance criteria:', '## Acceptance criteria', 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended'; the `check_reading_acceptance` doc contains '[`check_request_parts`]'.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs. Request 'Do three things:' with '(1) Add the --json flag to status', '(2) Document the flag in the guide', '(3) Cover the flag with a timeout test', inline and as separate lines; all three name 'flag' on purpose. Base reading from `terms_reading` (reading.rs:7293, wraps `governed_reading` 4635) with deliverables src/status.rs and docs/guide.md and criteria '[behavior] status --json prints json' and '[content] docs/guide.md documents the flag'. (a) part 3 absent: `refuser_for(&reading, request)` (reading.rs:7288) returns Some("check_request_parts"). (b) part 3 only in `out_of_scope` as a follow-up: same. (c) criterion '[behavior] a test fails when the timeout is missing' added: None and `check_reading_acceptance` Ok. (d) '(2) Reject future timestamps' dropped: refused. (e) criterion 'Later retries reject future timestamps': accepted. (f) 'Part (3) is out of scope for this job' added to (a): still refused. (g) 'Part (3) timeout test will be added later': still refused. (h) 'The timeout test is deferred': still refused. (i) part '(2) Report skipped checks in status' with criterion 'status lists skipped checks': covered. (j) 'Part (2) skipped checks are omitted': ignored, error names it and 'omitted'. (k) criterion 'a reading that moves the flag to a follow-up job is refused, and the timeout test passes' added to (a): accepted (the follow-up clause holds no distinctive stem of part 3). (l) 'the timeout test is moved to a follow-up job': refused. (m) the same reading with deliverable tests/timeout.rs added and no criterion: still refused (path alone does not cover; see criterion 3). A request Acceptance bullet dropped: refused (Bullet case, two bullets, one without a criterion).
